threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for 'the tube' like it's the only transport option. Everyone else knows it's all about the bus or cycling here.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the entire bus with 90s R&B, and somehow we all just leaned in instead of rolling our eyes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a busker playing accordions while a couple argued over a flammkuchen at the corner of Schillerkiez. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop competing for your attention with a Michelin-starred vegan joint, all while the Spree flows by.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local by the way they react to the BART delays—we barely flinch. Tourists look like deer in headlights when the trains get funky.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni driver stopping to help a lost tourist with a map today. Not something you see every day in the chaos of the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars are supposed to serve tapas, but many locals prefer a simple bocadillo over the fancy platters. It's not all about sharing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with the T-10 card at the metro, unsure if it’s valid for that trip or if they need to validate it again.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'Dalston Junction' like a tourist, not 'Dalston' when you mean the station. Locals know better, we just glide in and out.
Caught the 35 from Brixton after midnight, overheard a guy ranting about how the last curry shop closed too early. Classic. You just can't beat those late-night munchies.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard an opera singer performing next to a kebab shop at 3 AM, I knew I was home in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a beer from a Späti and sit on the steps of an old factory while street performers turn the evening into a mini fest.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local when they’ve got a go-to burrito spot that they defend like it’s family. And they don’t break eye contact while ordering.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 at the corner of Jones and O’Farrell—two guys arguing over the window seat. Lasted the whole ride, a real show of San Francisco drama.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think locals just sip café amb llet at terraces all day, but real Gràcians hustle between markets, kids’ schools, and errands.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still pull out a map at Sagrada Família, trying to figure out which way to go. The locals just use their phones now.
